caption: Substitutable reasoning. Two alternative engines use a domain’s task and operation models while making different planning decisions. Model selection chooses a foundation model within an engine; controlled application and acceptance consume their own models and evidence. Type compatibility preserves the request form, not semantic quality or equivalent behavior.
conversion: Author-approved model-centered appendix revision: two new compact architecture figures aligned with settled five-model inventories, plus targeted model-role clarifications in the existing mutation and delegation figures.
svg_title: Substitutable reasoning with stable domain obligations
svg_description: Task and workflow models guide two alternative engines: a pass-graph executor or a planning agent. Capability and selection knowledge informs model choice within an engine. Both engines produce typed proposals governed by an operation model and applied to the current artifact through a controlled application boundary. Separate evaluation and an acceptance model guide acceptance. Restricting mutation authority requires more than a typed request interface.
